credential.title: One-time setup
credential.why: Homey does not let an app create Flows on its own, so Lightkeeper needs an API key from you. It uses the key only to build and maintain the Flows behind this device — nothing else.
credential.step2: Settings → API Keys → New API Key
credential.step3: Tick the Flow permissions, then create it
credential.step4: Copy the key and paste it here
credential.malformed: That does not look like a complete API key. Copy the whole key shown when you create it.
credential.expired: The API key is no longer valid. Create a new one in the Homey Web App and enter it here.
credential.noScope: This key works, but it cannot create Flows. Make a new one with the Flow permissions ticked — permissions cannot be added to a key afterwards.
credential.unreachable: Could not reach Homey to check the API key. Try again in a moment.

source.reattach: __name__ looks like the same remote, re-added. Re-attaching keeps every mapping and target exactly as they were.
source.reattachAmbiguous: __count__ remotes look like this one, so Lightkeeper cannot tell which it was. Open repair and choose the right one — your mappings and lights are kept either way.

state.noConfiguration: This Light Remote has no configuration. Repair it to set it up again.
state.needsCredential: Lightkeeper needs a new API key to manage its Flows.
state.sourceGone: The remote this device listens to is no longer paired.
state.surfaceChanged: This remote now exposes different events. Open repair to remap it.
state.noTargets: None of this device's lights are available.
state.noTargetsResponding: __count__ light(s) are not responding to Lightkeeper. Check that they are powered on.
state.someTargetsNotResponding: __count__ of __total__ lights are not responding. Check that they are powered on.
state.unsupportedMapping: Lightkeeper could not build a Flow for __controls__. Open Repair and assign that control to something else.
state.flowEdited: A Flow this app generated has been edited by hand. Open repair to rebuild it.
state.noSchedule: This schedule has no configuration. Repair it to set it up again.
state.noTimeCard: This Homey does not offer a time trigger Lightkeeper can build on, so the schedule cannot be created. Please report this at github.com/thomassidor/lightkeeper/issues with your firmware version.
state.noTimezone: Lightkeeper cannot read this Homey's timezone, so time-based lighting is paused. Restart the app and report this if it persists.
state.noCurve: This light has no configuration. Repair it to set it up again.
state.noWarmthTargets: None of this device's lights can change their warmth, so there is nothing for it to do.
state.noDaylight: This light has no configuration. Repair it to set it up again.
state.noDimTargets: None of this device's lights can change their brightness, so there is nothing for it to do.
state.daylightFeedback: These lamps are brightening the sensor this device reads, so they keep raising their own brightness. Move the sensor away from their light, or lower the brightness at the bright end.
state.daylightSensorStale: __name__ has not reported for __hours__ hours, so these lights are held where they are. A few quiet hours are normal, but a sensor silent this long has probably stopped — check its battery, or repair this device to pick another sensor.
state.noDaylightSource: Lightkeeper cannot tell how light it is: no light sensor is reporting, and this Homey has not told it where it is. Add a light sensor in Repair, or set your Homey's location.
state.persistFailed: Lightkeeper could not save what it learned about its Flows. Open repair to try again.
state.invalidConfiguration: This device's stored configuration is not one Lightkeeper can read. Repair it to set it up again.
state.configurationFromNewerVersion: This device was set up by a newer version of Lightkeeper. Update the app; its settings are safe and will be read again.
state.sourceUnavailable: Homey reports that this remote is unavailable.
state.flowCleanup: An older Flow could not be removed. Lightkeeper will retry; duplicate actions may occur until cleanup succeeds.

settings.evidenceHelp: Record seven days on Homey, including restarts, sensor readings, light reports and control decisions. No computer needs to stay on. The recording stops after seven days or at 64 MB; existing evidence is kept. Nothing is sent elsewhere.
settings.evidenceExportHelp: Export the full recording from your computer with the command below. The ordinary bug report includes status only. Export and clear the existing recording before starting another test.
settings.evidenceSummary: __state__. __records__ saved records, __megabytes__ MB, __dropped__ dropped records. Scheduled end: __end__.
settings.apiKeyExplain: Homey does not let an app create Flows on its own, so Lightkeeper needs an API key from you. Create one at my.homey.app → Settings → API Keys with Flow permissions. Your existing devices keep working without it — only the Flows behind them stop being maintained.
settings.keyValid: A working API key is saved.
settings.keyMissing: No API key saved yet. Lightkeeper cannot create its Flows without one.
settings.keyBroken: The saved API key is not working.
settings.clockUnresolved: Lightkeeper could not read the Homey's timezone, so this schedule will not fire.
settings.noControllers: No Light Remotes yet. Add one from Devices.
settings.flowsExplain: Lightkeeper creates a Flow for each mapped button, and two for each schedule window. Flows whose Lightkeeper device no longer exists are orphans and can be deleted safely — only Flows this app created for a device that no longer exists are touched.
settings.orphansFound: __orphans__ orphaned Flow(s) out of __total__ generated, across __live__ live Lightkeeper device(s).
settings.sweepRefused: __total__ generated Flow(s) found, but no Lightkeeper device is running right now. Every Flow would look orphaned, so nothing will be deleted. Check your Lightkeeper devices first.
settings.sweepStale: The list changed while it was on screen, so nothing was deleted. Here it is again.
settings.sweepUnreadable: Lightkeeper could not list its own devices just now, so it cannot tell which Flows are orphaned. Nothing was deleted. Reload this page in a moment.
settings.sweepNotApproved: That request did not name which Flows to delete, so nothing was deleted. Reload this page and use the button.
settings.sweepUnmanaged: __unmanaged__ Flow(s) use a Lightkeeper card but were not created by this app, so they are left alone.
settings.sweeping: Deleting… this can take a while for hundreds of Flows.
settings.pressesExplain: Press a button on your remote, then reload this page. If nothing appears, the generated Flow is not firing. If a row appears but says it was ignored, the reason is shown.
settings.writesExplain: What the app actually sent to each light. An accepted press with no write here means the press was understood but never reached a light.
settings.requestFailed: The request could not be completed. Try again.
settings.noSchedules: No schedules yet. Add one from Devices.
settings.scheduleNoEntries: This schedule has no times set. Repair it to add some.
settings.noDaylight: No Room-sensing Lights are set up.
settings.daylightSky: The sun is __degrees__° above the horizon
settings.daylightNoLocation: This Homey has not said where it is
settings.daylightNoLocationHelp: Without a location Lightkeeper cannot work out where the sun is, so a Room-sensing Light needs a light sensor instead. Set your location in Homey’s own settings.
settings.daylightNoSensors: No light sensors are being read.
settings.daylightNow: Holding these lights at __percent__%, from the __source__.
settings.daylightUnknown: It cannot tell how light it is, so it is leaving these lights alone.
settings.daylightUsingSky: Following the sun; no light sensors chosen.
settings.daylightFeedbackPossible: These lights can brighten the sensor they read, so watch for them creeping up. If they do, move the sensor out of their light or lower the brightness at the bright end.
settings.daylightFeedbackSeen: Seen __count__ of 5 times: the reading rose just after these lights did. At 5 this device will say so on its tile. Move the sensor out of their light, or lower the brightness at the bright end.
settings.noCircadian: No circadian or Colour Curve Lights yet. Add one from Devices.
settings.circadianNow: Now at __warmth__% warmth, next point at __next__
settings.circadianNowBetween: Now between __from__ and __to__, next point at __next__
settings.circadianPreStageOff: Setting the colour before the lights come on was turned off automatically: one of these lights switched itself on.
settings.publishOnly: Works out what its lights should be, and leaves them alone until a remote or a Flow asks.

lights.title: Which lights?
lights.emptyBody: Lightkeeper uses lights already in Homey. Add a bulb or a lamp first, then come back.

intro.circadianTitle: Warm at night, cool at noon
intro.circadianBlurb: Your lights follow the sun instead of sitting at one colour all day.
intro.curveBlurb: Set a colour at the times that matter. The day fades between them.
intro.daylightTitle: Dim when the daylight does the work
intro.daylightBlurb: Your lamps fill in whatever daylight is missing — measured by a sensor, or worked out from the sun.
intro.scheduleBlurb: Pick the hours they should be on.
intro.controllerBlurb: Give each button on a remote a job, without building a Flow for every press.
intro.theDayWhy: How bright and how warm each part of the day is
intro.theCurveWhy: Start from a set and change the points that matter
intro.theSensorWhy: One light sensor if you have one, the sun’s height if you don’t
intro.theResponseWhy: How bright the lamps go when the room is dark, and when it is bright
intro.theBlocksWhy: Set the hours they switch on and off
intro.theButtonsWhy: The usual jobs are filled in already

review.title: Ready to add
review.nowFromSun: right now, with the sun __degrees__° above the horizon

control.title: How Lightkeeper controls your lights
control.after: Change lights after they turn on
control.afterWhy: Lights can turn on in their previous colour and change a moment later.
control.afterBrightnessWhy: Lights can turn on at their previous brightness and change a moment later.
control.before: Set lights before they turn on
control.beforeWhy: Lights turn on in the right colour. Needs a quick test first, as some lights turn on when they are set.
control.noneWhy: Lightkeeper calculates colour and brightness but leaves your lights alone. Use the values in your own flows.
control.testNote: Takes about 15 seconds. Each light blinks once, then goes back to how it was.
control.passed: Turns on in the right colour
control.fallback: Turned on when set, so it is changed after it turns on
control.testedNow: Tested just now · __count__ lights back to how they were
control.testedNowOne: Tested just now · the light is back to how it was
control.testedNowSome: Tested just now · __restored__ of __count__ lights back to how they were
control.testedBefore: From the last test. Lights added since then are changed after they turn on until they are tested.
control.testFailed: The test could not be run. Check that the lights are reachable and try again.

tip.daylight: Want more control? Use the Room-sensing light from Lightkeeper.

day.title: Colour through the day
day.todayFixed: No sunrise to follow here, so these hours are fixed: __sunrise__ and __sunset__

remote.title: Which remote?
remote.none: No remotes or switches found. Add one to Homey first.
remote.noMatch: No device of that name. Check the spelling, or clear the search.
remote.otherWhy: Homey has heard no button press from the rest of the house.
remote.unusable: Nothing can be read from __name__, so it cannot drive anything. Pick another.
remote.reattachText: The remote this device used has gone. __name__ looks like the same kind of device.

blocks.title: When are they on?
blocks.overlapMeans: The later one wins while they overlap. Nothing breaks — the lights simply stay on through both.

tryit.title: See any time of day
tryit.help: Drag to a time, then show it on the lamps.

sensor.title: Where should the reading come from?
sensor.aSensorWhy: Measures the light in the room itself.
sensor.theSunWhy: No sensor needed. Works perfectly well on its own.
sensor.noPosition: Homey has not been told where it is
sensor.noneFound: No light sensors on this Homey — the sun it is.

response.title: How bright should the lamps be?
response.whenSun: When does this room get its sun?
response.whenSunWhy: Pick the part of the day when direct light reaches it.
response.followingSunMeans: The lamps ease off as this room’s own light arrives, and it shifts with the season on its own.
response.tried: Set __writes__ light(s) to what the room asks for right now.

week.noHistory: No readings to show yet, so the numbers below start from the defaults.
week.usable: A clear day and night pattern.
week.usableDetail: __night__ lx at night, __noon__ lx around noon — plenty to act on.
week.flatDetail: __low__ to __high__ lx — nothing to act on. Try a sensor in a room that gets daylight, or have the lights follow the sun instead.
week.nothing: Nothing reported in the last seven days.
week.quietMeans: It reported normally until __when__, then stopped — and a stopped sensor holds your lights at one brightness. Try a different sensor, or have the lights follow the sun instead.

job.lightkeeperBlurb: Turn on with level and warmth from other Lightkeeper devices.
job.lightkeeperChosen: Reads these setups at the moment of the press
job.takeBlurb: Read at the moment of the press, not fixed now.
job.swatchNote: Swatches show what each setup is producing right now.
job.levelNote: Levels are what each setup is calling for right now.
job.noSources: No other Lightkeeper devices yet. Add a circadian light, a Colour Curve Light, a schedule or a Room-sensing Light, and this button can follow it.
job.needASource: Choose at least one setup to take a colour or a brightness from.

sourceWarn.keepsUpdated: __name__ keeps its own lights up to date as well.
sourceWarn.sharedMeans: __count__ of this button’s lights are also driven by __name__, so both will set them when they come on and they may step between the two. Choose “Don’t change lights automatically” on __name__, or give this button a plain On.
sourceWarn.ownMeans: It will go on setting its own lights through the day, whatever this button does.
